stories.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
stories.synopsis: Scientists have used AI to make experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. For people who lost their sight to an inherited eye disease or an accident, it brings the hope of seeing again one step closer.

stories.title: Using AI to map disaster damage for faster rescue and recovery
stories.synopsis: Texas A&M's CLARKE system can assess up to 2,000 homes in seven minutes, even without an internet connection after a drone lands. Researchers estimate it could help emergency managers make decisions roughly a day earlier so help reaches the hardest-hit areas first. It is already part of the standard operating procedure for Florida's disaster drone team.

stories.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
stories.synopsis: MIT researchers have developed a technique for building fast, trustworthy and adaptable AI climate emulators using only a fraction of the data typically required. These models can run in just a few seconds, which lets scientists explore many future climate scenarios quickly. The team hopes the work will make such tools more useful for policy decisions.

stories.title: 'Digital advances are reshaping nature conservation' say experts
stories.synopsis: Kew Gardens' State of the World's Plants and Fungi 2026 report, which draws on more than 400 scientists from 40 countries, finds that AI is helping to identify challenging plants and even pinpoint species new to science. Specimens are now being analysed at an unprecedented scale, and Kew has digitised 7.4 million plant and fungi specimens. The authors note that AI identifications still need expert validation, but it's a hopeful sign for the race to protect nature.

stories.title: AlphaGenome 2: Google's New AI Gets Better at Decoding Disease-Linked DNA
stories.synopsis: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on Nov. 11. It is a DNA analysis model that predicts how genetic variations affect individual cell types. Trained on more than 107 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, it identified 30% of causal variants in one benchmark, up from 16% for the original version. That could bring real benefits to drug research.

stories.title: AI Summit explores technology's role in student success, equity
stories.synopsis: More than 90 educators from Michigan and several other states gathered for Kent ISD's fourth annual AI Summit in early November. The aim was to explore how AI can make learning more accessible and engaging for students while simplifying teachers' work. Sessions stressed being open with students about when and why AI is used, so they learn to use it well.

stories.title: AI medicine breakthrough: Could 'good viruses' created by AI cure deadly diseases and infections?
stories.synopsis: For the first time, scientists say they have used AI-designed viruses called phages to treat a person with a life-threatening E. coli infection that had resisted antibiotics and every phage doctors could find. The startup Radical Numerics used an AI model called Omnii to redesign a phage known as T7. Outside experts are intrigued but cautious, and results could take months, but it's a hopeful step against drug-resistant infections.

stories.title: AI Detects "Invisible" Signs of Pancreatic Cancer Years Before Diagnosis
stories.synopsis: A new AI system called REDMOD can pick up extremely subtle changes in pancreatic tissue that may signal cancer long before it is visible on conventional scans. It spotted warning signs an average of 475 days before diagnosis and was nearly twice as sensitive as experienced radiologists. The research appeared in the journal Gut, and more study is needed before routine use, but it points toward earlier, potentially lifesaving treatment.

stories.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a "natural Ozempic" with a surprising advantage
stories.synopsis: Stanford Medicine scientists used AI to search 20,000 human genes for new hormones. They identified a naturally occurring molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals. It could lead to a new generation of weight-loss medications.

stories.title: Mayo Clinic AI detects pancreatic cancer up to 3 years before diagnosis in landmark validation study
stories.synopsis: A Mayo Clinic AI model called REDMOD helps specialists spot pancreatic cancer on routine abdominal CT scans up to three years before clinical diagnosis. In a study of nearly 2,000 scans that were originally read as normal, it identified 73% of the prediagnostic cancers about 16 months ahead of diagnosis, nearly double the rate of specialists working without AI. The team is now moving the work into clinical testing, which is hopeful news for earlier treatment of a very hard-to-catch cancer.

stories.title: AI is changing cancer treatment — and a new breakthrough shows just how far we've come
stories.synopsis: Researchers are using AI to understand cancer in far more detail than was possible a decade ago, moving toward treatments matched to the genetic makeup of each person's tumor. One example is the National Cancer Institute's PERCEPTION tool, which reads gene activity in individual cancer cells to predict whether certain drugs might work. The article is clear that lab and patient testing still come next, but it sees encouraging signs for more personalized care.

stories.title: AI Forecasts Heart Patients' Survival Slightly Better Than Doctors
stories.synopsis: In a study of 27,382 heart patients in the UK and US, an AI program measured heart function from scans in just three to four seconds. Its numbers also tracked which patients later survived slightly better than the doctors' own readings. Doctors still came out ahead for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which points to AI and clinicians working well as a team.

stories.title: AI medicine breakthrough: Could 'good viruses' created by AI, cure deadly viruses?
stories.synopsis: For the first time, scientists say they have used viruses designed by AI, called phages, to treat a person with a life-threatening E. coli infection that hadn't responded to antibiotics or any phage doctors could find. The startup Radical Numerics used an AI model called Omnii to redesign a phage so it could grab onto the patient's resistant strain, and the FDA authorized a trial. Results could take months, but the company hopes to one day build a custom phage for a patient in just days.

stories.title: How AI glasses are changing the way people communicate
stories.synopsis: AI glasses are moving from gadget to everyday tool for travellers and people with hearing loss. Liu Shanshan, who lost her hearing at age three, uses glasses that show speech as captions almost in real time, and says she would wear them at meetings, while eating out, or when hailing a taxi. Others are using real-time translation to speak in their own language and still be understood.

stories.title: Environmental groups embrace AI, even as they warn of data center impacts
stories.synopsis: Environmental groups around the world are using AI to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife, including Save the Elephants researchers flying surveillance drones in Kenya's Samburu National Reserve. With the climate and biodiversity crises growing more urgent, these groups say AI helps them move faster and make better use of the information they collect. Some, like the World Resources Institute, are also using AI carefully to keep its own footprint small.
